To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
context information affects early and late ERP components, and that this effect depends on the valence of the context and on self-reference.
the perception of faces is influenced by context information, especially if this context information is related to the self and is socially threatening.
the processing of neutral faces is modulated by the context, i.e. the affective valence of the context information and the reference of the information.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of context information on visual processing of faces.
the impact of verbally provided context information on the early perceptual processing of facial stimuli.
the influence of context information on the visual processing of human faces.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
self-related information is processed automatically and that affective information influences later stages of face processing.

context information affects early perceptual processing and later cognitive stages, with self-referenced context information having a stronger effect on early stages, whereas the effect of valence increases with later stages.
the processing of facial expressions and faces is modulated in different ways, depending on the type of context information and the processing stage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the processing of faces is not only modulated by the affective valence of context information but also by reference.
self-relevance and valence of context information have different effects on the processing of neutral faces.
the processing of a face is affected by the affective valence of context information and by the reference (self vs. other) of the context information.
The main takeaway from our work is that
context information can have an impact on the processing of human faces, which is of particular importance for understanding how context information affects social interactions.
context information can have an impact on the processing of human faces at early processing stages.

the processing of faces is not only affected by context information about the person but also by the reference (self-referential or other-referential) and the valence (neutral, physically and socially threatening) of the information.
